references.text: Mount Sinai was shrouded in smoke because the Lord descended on it in fire, and Moses spoke with God who answered him with a voice. This is the historical event referred to in Deuteronomy 4:33.

The people saw the thunder and the flames and heard the sound of the trumpet, and they asked Moses to speak to them instead of God, because they feared dying. This confirms that the people heard God's voice and survived.
The glory of the Lord was like a consuming fire on top of the mountain for the children of Israel. This describes the fire from which God spoke.
The Lord spoke with the people face to face on the mountain, right out of the fire. A parallel account in Deuteronomy that repeats the same point.

The people acknowledge that they have seen that God speaks with humans right out of the fire, and they are still alive. They ask who has ever heard the voice of the living God from the fire and survived.
Hebrews refers to the Sinai experience with fire, darkness, and a voice that spoke, where those who heard begged that no more words be spoken to them.
